# Blueprint nodes

<div class="gen-note">Generated from the APS 3.0 source code: every name, pin, default and description below is read from the plugin itself, so it matches what you see in the editor.</div>

Every APS node you can place in a Blueprint graph, grouped by where it lives. **Green** nodes are pure (no white execution pins: they only read), **blue** nodes do something, **red** ones are events you override. Pins are coloured as in the editor. Search this page with [[Ctrl]] + [[F]], or the site search above: every node is in it.

## APS Core
The component on every AI. Its nodes read what the AI believes and change how it behaves. Drag from an APS Core reference, or right-click in its owner's graph and type the node's name.

## APS Perception Listener

### Stimulus
<div class="bpn-list"><div class="bpn call" id="n-apssubsystem-emitstimulus" data-search="Emit Stimulus" data-text="Emit a stimulus to all AI agents that can receive it. Pipeline (cheapest checks first): 1. Radius cull — agents beyond Event.Radius skipped 2. LOD tier — agents above Event.MaxLODTier skipped 3. Team filter — agents on same team as Source skipped (if bTeamFilter) 4. Wall trace — occlusion check if E"><div class="bpn-head"><span class="bpn-icon"></span><b>Emit Stimulus</b><span class="badge">library</span></div><div class="bpn-meta"><span>Callable</span> <span class="cat">APS › Stimulus</span></div><div class="bpn-pins"><div class="bpn-in"><span class="pin exec"><i></i></span><span class="pin struct" title="APSStimulus Event"><i></i><b>Event</b><small>APSStimulus Event</small></span></div><div class="bpn-out"><span class="pin exec"><i></i></span></div></div><div class="bpn-doc"><p>Emit a stimulus to all AI agents that can receive it.</p><p>Pipeline (cheapest checks first): 1. Radius cull — agents beyond Event.Radius skipped 2. LOD tier   — agents above Event.MaxLODTier skipped 3. Team filter — agents on same team as Source skipped (if bTeamFilter) 4. Wall trace  — occlusion check if Event.bRequiresClearPath 5. Deliver to PerceptionCore::ReceiveStimulus()</p><p>All senses that registered a matching tag prefix receive the event.</p><p>Use this for any stimulus that should be centrally filtered and distributed. Direct calls to ReportVibrationEvent / ReportSoundEvent bypass this pipeline.</p></div></div></div>

<p class="inert-why"><b>Not reachable from Blueprint in APS 3.0.</b> This is on the Vibration Sense object the APS Core creates, and no node returns it. Use the APS Core's <b>Report Vibration Event</b>, which does the same.</p>

## Smell Sense
<p class="inert-why"><b>Not reachable from Blueprint in APS 3.0.</b> This is on the Smell Sense object the APS Core creates, and no node returns it. For one kind of AI with its own wind, set <b>Wind Direction</b> in the Class Defaults of a Blueprint child of Smell Sense; for everyone, <b>Set Wind State</b> on the APS Subsystem.</p>

<div class="bpn-list"><div class="bpn call" id="n-smell-sense-setwinddirection" data-search="Set Wind Direction" data-text="Set this sense&#x27;s own wind direction, overriding the world&#x27;s. @param Direction World-space direction the wind is blowing TOWARD (the way the air moves). ## APSStance Provider
An interface: implement it on your character so APS can read its stance (standing, crouching, prone) from your own movement code.
